text: Good API design makes software easier to use and maintain. When building REST APIs, start by choosing clear, meaningful endpoints, such as /users or /orders, so developers understand what each one does. Always return the correct status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is missing, because this helps clients handle responses properly. Good documentation is also essential, since it explains how to use every endpoint with examples. Finally, plan for change by using versioning, for example /v1/users, so updates do not break existing applications. Following these practices keeps your API reliable and friendly for everyone.
